tagline: A leading global bank with strong roots in Germany, delivering sustainable value through four complementary business divisions: Corporate Bank, Investment Bank, Private Bank, and Asset Management.
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the primary performance indicator for a global bank like Deutsche Bank, reflecting capital-adjusted profitability on tangible shareholders' equity. It captures the efficiency of strategic transformation and operational discipline, both essential in the financial services sector.

kpis.short: Post-tax return on average tangible shareholders' equity
kpis.name: Post-tax return on average tangible shareholders' equity
kpis.explanation: Measures the return on tangible shareholders' equity after taxes, a key performance indicator for banks.
kpis.description: The ratio reached 10.3% in 2025, exceeding targets and showing significant improvement versus 2024.
kpis.signal: Best tangible equity return in the group's history.

kpis.name: Total net revenues
kpis.explanation: Total revenues after deduction of interest paid, the primary revenue driver for the bank.
kpis.description: Revenues reached EUR 32.1 billion in 2025, up 7% versus 2024, in line with strategic objectives.
kpis.signal: Sixth consecutive year of revenue growth.

kpis.name: Cost/income ratio
kpis.explanation: Non-interest expenses as a share of total revenues, a measure of operational efficiency.
kpis.description: The ratio improved from 76.3% in 2024 to 64.4% in 2025, driven by rigorous cost management and revenue growth.

kpis.name: Pre-provision profit
kpis.explanation: Profit generated before provisions for credit losses, an indicator of operational performance.
kpis.description: Pre-provision profit reached EUR 11.4 billion in 2025, compared to EUR 7.1 billion in 2024.

kpis.name: Net interest margin
kpis.explanation: Spread between interest revenue earned and interest costs paid, expressed as a percentage of productive assets.
kpis.description: Net interest margin improved to 1.5% in 2025 from 1.3% in 2024, supported by the rate environment.
kpis.signal: Improved net interest margin in a higher rate environment.

kpis.name: Common Equity Tier 1 ratio
kpis.explanation: Financial strength indicator, measuring the quality of capital relative to risk-weighted assets.
kpis.description: The CET1 ratio stood at 14.2% in 2025, exceeding regulatory requirements and reflecting prudent capital management.

kpis.name: Employees (full-time equivalent)
kpis.explanation: Total number of full-time equivalent employees across the group.
kpis.description: Headcount stood at 89,879 full-time equivalents in 2025, slightly up from 89,753 in 2024.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of EUR 1,435.07 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Sustainable finance volume
kpis.explanation: Annual volume of financings and investments related to sustainability.
kpis.description: Volume reached EUR 98 billion in 2025, up from EUR 93 billion in 2024, reflecting the group's commitment to ecological transition.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth in sustainable finance activities.

kpis.name: Number of branches
kpis.explanation: Total number of physical banking network locations.
kpis.description: Branch count declined to 1,179 in 2025 from 1,307 in 2024, consistent with modernization and digitalization strategy.
kpis.signal: Continued reduction of physical footprint in favor of digital channels.

risks.title: Third-party vendor dependencies
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned in the report via third-party vendor risks and receives heightened attention from the Risk Committee. The language is precise and repeated, indicating ongoing concern. Technology is a strategic category for the bank. The risk is stable but central to regulatory discussions.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and IT posture
risks.score_rationale: The Management Board regularly presents detailed cybersecurity reports to the Supervisory Board, with the subject addressed across multiple committees. The intensity of oversight and frequency of reporting indicate a high-level risk, integrated into the resilience strategy.

risks.title: Regulatory compliance and remediation
risks.score_rationale: The text repeatedly mentions remediation of regulatory orders, discussions with regulators, and SREP engagement. The language is concerned and repetitive, showing a structural major risk for the bank, with high weight in governance priorities.

risks.title: Operational model transformation
risks.score_rationale: Optimization of the target operating model is a recurring theme in Supervisory Board discussions. The risk is strategic, linked to transformation implementation. The language is proactive but reflects high complexity.

risks.title: Leadership stability and governance
risks.score_rationale: The text details several key management changes (CRO, CFO, Americas leadership). James von Moltke's departure after 9 years and successor appointments signal a major transition risk. The language is cautious, emphasizing continuity importance.

risks.title: High-risk litigation
risks.score_rationale: The Risk Committee now monitors high-risk litigation following dissolution of the Regulatory Oversight Committee. The subject is flagged as a priority, with direct governance oversight. The weight is high in terms of reputation and potential costs.

risks.title: Resilience amid geopolitical tensions
risks.score_rationale: The Chairman explicitly mentions geopolitical tensions as a central challenge. The language is forward-looking and concerned. This risk is stable but amplified by commercial and regional conflicts noted in reports.

risks.title: Real estate sector risks
risks.score_rationale: Commercial real estate is mentioned as an impact area in Risk Committee analyses. The language is measured, but the subject is recurrent. The risk is moderate but tied to specific exposures.

ai_positioning.summary: Deutsche Bank does not display pronounced positioning on artificial intelligence in the document. The emphasis is on general technology transformation, without specific mention of AI initiatives or dedicated investments.
evidence: No mention of generative AI or concrete applications in the report.
Technology investments are cited as self-funded, but without detail on AI.
No reference to partnerships, products, or APIs related to AI.
